first_fault: - The text states that the acid soluble pool contains the small molecules (micromolecules), but then says "The acid insoluble fraction also contains carbohydrates and lipids" and "Together with proteins and nucleic acids, these comprise the true macromolecular fraction of any living tissue or cell." This is contradictory because carbohydrates and lipids are explicitly stated to be in the acid insoluble fraction, yet the first sentence of the Key points says "The acid soluble pool contains micromolecules."
said:
VERDICT: fail
- The text states that the acid soluble pool contains the small molecules (micromolecules), but then says "The acid insoluble fraction also contains carbohydrates and lipids" and "Together with proteins and nucleic acids, these comprise the true macromolecular fraction of any living tissue or cell." This is contradictory because carbohydrates and lipids are explicitly stated to be in the acid insoluble fraction, yet the first sentence of the Key points says "The acid soluble pool contains micromolecules."
- The text states that lipids make up 2 percent, carbohydrates 3 percent, proteins 10 to 15 percent, and nucleic acids 5 to 7 percent. The sum of these given percentages is 2 + 3 + 10 + 15 + 5 + 7 = 42 percent, which leaves 58 percent unaccounted for, but the text earlier said ions make up the remaining 1 percent (after 70-90% water, 10-15% proteins, 3% carbs, 2% lipids, 5-7% nucleic acids).
- The text says "Together with proteins and nucleic acids, these comprise the true macromolecular fraction," but lipids are not macromolecules by the definition given earlier (macromolecules are 10,000 daltons or more).
- The text says "The acid insoluble fraction also contains carbohydrates and lipids," but earlier it said "The acid insoluble fraction contains the large molecules" (macromolecules), and carbohydrates are not large molecules by the size definition (they are small molecules).
- The text says "The acid insoluble fraction also contains carbohydrates and lipids" and "Together with proteins and nucleic acids, these comprise the true macromolecular fraction," but carbohydrates and lipids are not macromolecules.
- The text says "According to the average composition of cells, water is the most abundant chemical, making up 70 to 90 percent," then lists proteins, carbohydrates, lipids, nucleic acids, and ions. The sum of the non-water percentages (10-15 + 3 + 2 + 5-7 + 1 = 21 to 26 percent) does not add up to the remaining 10 to 30 percent, and the ion percentage is stated as 1 percent but the sum of the listed percentages (10 to 15 + 3 + 2 + 5 to 7 = 20 to 25) already exceeds the remaining 10 to 30 percent when water is 70 to 90 percent.
- The text says "Lipids are small molecules. Their molecular weights do not exceed 800 daltons. So why do they end up in the large, acid insoluble fraction?" but then in the Key points it says "Lipids are small molecules (under 800 Da) but appear in the acid insoluble fraction because they form cell membranes that break into water-insoluble vesicles." This is consistent, but the worked example says "Finally, imagine she finds a lipid with a molecular weight of 700 daltons. Even though this is a small molecule, it will likely end up in the acid insoluble fraction when the tissue is ground." This is consistent with the text, but the text earlier said "The acid insoluble fraction contains the large molecules" and "The acid insoluble fraction also contains carbohydrates and lipids," which is inconsistent because carbohydrates and lipids are not large molecules.
- The text says "Together, these two groups of molecules represent the entire chemical composition of living tissues," but the text also mentions water, ions, and other chemicals, so this is an overstatement.
- The text says "Proteins are essential for life. They are called polypeptides." but a polypeptide is a chain of amino acids, and a protein can be a single polypeptide or multiple, but the text says "A protein is a linear chain of amino acids," which is oversimplified but not contradictory.
- The text says "The other type of macromolecule in the acid insoluble fraction is the nucleic acid," but earlier it said "The acid insoluble fraction contains the large molecules" and "The acid insoluble fraction also contains carbohydrates and lipids," so nucleic acids are not the only macromolecule in the acid insoluble fraction; proteins are also there.
- The text says "Carbohydrates and lipids make up a smaller percentage of the cell compared to proteins and nucleic acids," but the numbers given (carbohydrates 3%, lipids 2%) are indeed smaller than proteins (10-15%) and nucleic acids (5-7%), so this is consistent.
- The text says "Ions make up the remaining 1 percent," but the sum of the listed percentages (10-15 + 3 + 2 + 5-7 = 20 to 27) plus 1 percent is 21 to 28 percent, which is less than the remaining 10 to 30 percent, so there is a discrepancy.
